name: Ketone monoester (R-1,3-butanediol ester)
lead: The ketone monoester (R)-3-hydroxybutyl (R)-3-hydroxybutyrate is a drink that raises blood D-beta-hydroxybutyrate quickly. It was developed at the US National Institutes of Health by Richard Veech and Todd King and later sold by companies including KetoneAid, TDeltaS and HVMN, according to Wikipedia. [1]
It is the best-studied exogenous ketone. Studies in healthy adults examined its kinetics and tolerability, effects on endurance fuel use in athletes, and appetite hormones. [2][3][4][5]
Its place in fat-loss discussions rests on one report of lower ghrelin and appetite; no published trial located in the sources reviewed tests it for fat loss or appearance.

paras: Healthy volunteers given the monoester in a meal-replacement drink showed raised plasma beta-hydroxybutyrate and acetoacetate; the study reported on kinetics, safety and tolerability. [2] A separate human study compared ketone drinks and the metabolism of exogenous ketones. [3] Unlike salts, esters lower blood pH, per Wikipedia. [1]

A 2016 paper reported that a ketone ester altered fuel preference and examined endurance performance in 39 high-performance athletes across five studies. [4] A 2018 study reported that a ketone ester drink lowered ghrelin and appetite in humans. [5] A 2020 study examined diet effects on brain network stability. [6] Mouse studies have tested ketone esters in Alzheimer's disease and cancer models, and a single case report described its use in an Alzheimer's patient. [7][8][9]

Human trials include the pharmacokinetics and tolerability studies and the athlete and appetite studies above. [2][4][5] Registered trials include ketone esters in heart failure, sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy, polycystic kidney disease, ageing and senescent T cells, nocturnal blood pressure, cerebrospinal fluid ketone levels and hypoxic tolerance. [10][11][12][13][14][15] No studies found on fat loss or appearance.

card.summary: The most-studied ketone drink; it lowers appetite hormones in one study, but fat-loss results are unpublished.

quick.overview:
The ketone monoester is a drink that quickly raises blood beta-hydroxybutyrate. It was developed at the NIH and sold under brands such as KetoneAid.

Human studies cover kinetics, endurance and appetite; fat loss and appearance have not been tested in published trials found here.
quick.mechanism: It is broken down into ketone bodies the body can use as fuel, raising blood ketones without fasting or dieting.
quick.risks: The 2012 study reported on tolerability in healthy adults. Long-term effects in healthy dieters are not established.
